clue.text: Show embarrassment about one that's somewhat indecent?

indicators.note: about says the word for reddening goes round the letter for one

parts.note: to blush is to go red with embarrassment
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look ashamed over a slightly rude person or joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps BLUSH round I. Blue means indecent, as in a blue joke, so the -ish form is 'somewhat indecent'; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is slang for risqué or smutty, and the suffix -ish waters it down to slightly so.

clue.text: Better way, we hear, to produce vegetable

indicators.note: we hear says the two words are taken by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: to better someone is to beat them, and a way is a route: said together, beat route

explanation.surface: A gardener has heard of a superior method for growing a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is a verb, to beat; 'way' is a route. 'we hear' has the pair spoken as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a dark red root grown for the table.

clue.text: Form of employment wise person got after university

indicators.note: got after places the wise person behind the letter for university

parts.note: a sage is a person of great wisdom

explanation.surface: A clever graduate finds a job once the degree is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got after' puts SAGE behind U. 'Employment' here is not a job but the act of using something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the employment of a word or tool is the way it is used, its customary manner of use.

clue.text: Persuasively present a church as source of strength, supposedly

parts.note: to spin a story is to present it in a favourable, persuasive light

explanation.surface: A preacher is urged to sell the congregation on faith as what keeps them strong.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the cartoon sailor Popeye, whose muscles swell when he eats a can of this leaf; 'supposedly' admits the nutrition claim is a legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the leafy green is popularly credited with building muscle, thanks to Popeye and its reputed iron content.

clue.text: Man on board posted elsewhere

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a man on board a ship
a letter that has been posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A company director has been transferred to another office.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'board' suggests a boardroom or a chessboard, but it is a ship's deck: AB is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who is not here but away in another place.

clue.text: Didn't have to go to school, and got on

definitions.text: Didn't have to go to school
definitions.meaning: a pupil who lived in at school had no daily journey to make
stepped onto a ship, train or plane

explanation.definitionFit: A pupil living in at school has no journey there, and a passenger embarking has climbed aboard: two senses of one past tense.

clue.text: Unconventional type destroying entire 300?

indicators.note: destroying says the letters are broken up and put together differently

parts.note: taken as written
CCC is 300 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An oddball smashes a whole collection of three hundred things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' rearranges ENTIRE together with CCC, the Roman numeral for 300; the question mark excuses the numeral joining the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: an oddball whose behaviour departs from the norm.

clue.text: You and I backed away from the wrong crowd

indicators.note: away from says the letters are taken out of the two words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backed says the pronoun is turned round before it is removed

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Two friends retreat from a bad set of companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns WE into EW, and 'away from' removes that EW from THE WRONG, where it straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large mass of people packed together.

clue.text: Game I run badly, making a bloomer

indicators.note: badly says the letters before it are poorly arranged and need reordering

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An organiser handles a match poorly and commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges GAME I RUN. A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, but here it is simply a thing that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a plant that flowers, here a popular red or pink pot plant.

clue.text: Certain people, in essence, showing what rulers can do

indicators.note: in says the words for certain and people sit inside the word for essence

parts.note: the meat of a matter is its essence or substance
sure means certain
men in the general sense of people

explanation.surface: A select few, at heart, demonstrate the power that monarchs hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The rulers are not kings but the marked sticks used for drawing straight lines and finding lengths.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a marked straight-edge is used for finding lengths, which is the job named here.

clue.text: Treaty announcement in which leaders of America, china, and England, say, come together

indicators.note: an announcement is something spoken, so the phrase described is taken by its sound

parts.words: in which leaders of America, china, and England, say, come together
parts.note: the first letters A, C and E are musical notes, and notes sounded together make a chord: said as two words, a chord

explanation.surface: A pact is proclaimed as the heads of three nations meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announcement' gives the sound of 'a chord'. The leaders are first letters A, C and E, which as musical notes played together form a chord; 'say' marks them as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal agreement between states, as in a peace pact.

clue.text: French product Berliner oddly selected

indicators.note: oddly selected says only the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word are chosen

explanation.surface: A German picks out a French item in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft cheese made in the region east of Paris.

clue.text: Leaving a report about scholar at home

indicators.note: about says the word for a loud report goes round the scholar and the word for at home

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun going off
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone departs, putting down a document concerning an academic who is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The 'report' is not a document but the noise of a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deserting or giving up a person or place.

clue.text: Conservative is supposed to, in more mature rebuff

indicators.note: in says the word for is supposed to sits inside the word for more mature

parts.note: older means more mature
someone who is supposed to do a thing should do it

explanation.surface: A Tory is expected to deliver a snub in a more grown-up way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, and 'more mature' describes age, not behaviour. Giving someone this treatment is an idiom for snubbing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a deliberate show of unfriendliness, pointedly ignoring someone.

clue.text: Reckless fellow's absurd speed on bad road

indicators.note: absurd says the letters of the next word are in a nonsensical order to be put right

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bad says the letters of the last word are out of order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild driver goes ridiculously fast along a poor road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' and 'bad' each rearrange only the single word beside them, so there are two short anagrams, not one long one. The 's after fellow reads as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bold, violent outlaw who stops at nothing.

clue.text: Taking part in matches, I tantalizingly lost, so it's said

indicators.note: Taking part in says a stretch of letters is lifted from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A player enters several games and is narrowly, teasingly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking part in' lifts the answer from 'matcHES I TANTalizingly'. The definition leans on the proverb 'he who hesitates is lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverb: the person who wavers is, by the old saying, lost.

clue.text: Put on trains, or older form of transport

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on
a person who coaches a team trains it

explanation.surface: A rail company lays on extra services, or else some vintage vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' is a verb, not railway vehicles: one who trains a team coaches it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: horse-drawn public carriages that ran fixed routes before the railways.

clue.text: Any done incorrectly could get cross

indicators.note: incorrectly says the two words before it are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tasks carried out wrongly might earn a mark against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges ANY DONE. The 'cross' is not a mark on the page but an adjective for bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: irritated or angry.

clue.text: Money spent importing piano to excel in performance

indicators.note: importing says the word for money spent brings the letter for piano inside it

parts.note: an outlay is a sum of money spent
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Cash goes on shipping in a piano so a musician can shine on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' brings P into OUTLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to perform better than an opponent in a game.

clue.text: Gold held by John's successor for members of company

indicators.note: held by says the word for gold sits inside the name of the book

parts.note: Acts is the book that follows the Gospel of John in the New Testament
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Bullion is kept by the heir of a man called John on behalf of a firm's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is the container signal. John is the fourth Gospel, so his successor is the next book of the New Testament. The company is a theatre troupe, not a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the players who make up a theatrical troupe.

clue.text: Vet before big match — it helps to select the best player

definitions.text: it helps to select the best player

indicators.note: before places the word for vet ahead of the word for a big match

parts.note: to vet someone is to screen them, checking their background
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: An animal doctor checks a horse ahead of an important fixture to pick the top competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' gives the order. A big match in cricket or rugby is an international. The 'player' is a film performer, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a filmed audition used in casting to choose who gets a part.

clue.text: Pressure to broadcast match

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A television channel is being pushed to show a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to put two like things together.

clue.text: Basic fare from Sicily to Milan — no more first class

definitions.text: Basic fare from Sicily to Milan

parts.note: something that is no more is past, over and done
A is the top grade, first class

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the cheap ticket up the length of Italy no longer includes the best seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fare' is food, not a ticket price; Sicily to Milan spans Italy from south to north.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the staple food eaten the whole length of Italy.

clue.text: Traveller using tracks across Arab country

indicators.note: across says the letters for tracks span the name of the country, one on each side

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway, which runs on tracks
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A voyager follows trails through a Middle Eastern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' is the container signal. In Britain, Traveller is a name for a member of the Gypsy and Roma communities.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a member of the Roma people, traditionally itinerant and called Travellers in Britain.

clue.text: Take from capitalism any thing that'll bring the fortune you want?

definitions.text: thing that'll bring the fortune you want

indicators.note: Take from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grab from the market economy whatever will make them rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a lucky charm believed to bring good luck to its owner.

clue.text: Inferior rum used in sling

indicators.note: used in says the word for rum is placed inside the word for sling

parts.note: to shy is to sling or throw, as at a coconut shy
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A bartender puts cheap spirits into a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' is the container signal. Neither word is a drink: rum is old British slang for strange, and to sling is to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: poorly made, of low quality.

clue.text: Bullying type in authority ran things

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follow it

explanation.surface: A domineering boss in charge managed everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cruel, oppressive ruler or domineering person.
